Covered what events are captured, export options (S3, syslog, SIEM connectors), retention policies and configuration, RBAC/SSO implications, KMS/encryption details, and log integrity. Action: Redwood to share log schema and security docs and schedule POC for streaming logs to customer's SIEM/S3.

encryption & KMS: at-rest, in-transit, customer KMS options
transcript:
[00:00] Liam O'Connor: All right thanks everyone for joining, today it's the audit logs and admin activity review. quick round of intros?
[00:08] Rajiv Kumar: Rajiv, CISO at Oceana Finance. we'll mostly listen and then ask mapping questions.
[00:14] Emily Park: Emily, head of platform. i'm focused on retention and export to our S3 bucket and to Splunk.
[00:20] Carlos Mendez: Carlos, DevOps. I'll handle the SIEM side.
[00:24] Liam O'Connor: Great. Sana from my side?
[00:27] Sana Patel: Hi all, Sana Patel, Solutions Engineer. i'll walk through what's captured and how you can get logs out. bear with me if the auto-transcript munges some acronyms.
[00:36] [00:36] Sana Patel: high-level — we capture admin activity and admin-auditable events across the control plane and the inference plane. that includes admin logins, role and policy changes, user provisioning/deprovisioning, API key creation and rotation, model version changes, rollout changes like canary/A-B flags, and data export events.
[00:56] Rajiv Kumar: when you say data export events, is that about customer data being downloaded or config exports?
[01:00] Sana Patel: both. we log config exports, dataset exports, and also explicit model output export calls. each event has actor, IP, timestamp, request id, and if applicable, resource ids.
[01:10] Emily Park: what's the retention default?
[01:12] Sana Patel: default retention on hosted is 90 days, we offer options up to 365 days for enterprise contracts. for dedicated and private you can configure retention or forward to your archive. we can also support legal hold flags where logs are retained until release.
[01:28] Carlos Mendez: can we stream logs in real time to Splunk?
[01:31] Sana Patel: yes — we support streaming via syslog, HTTPS POST to customer endpoints, and S3 delivery (JSON lines). for Splunk specifically customers either ingest from S3 or we push via HTTP Event Collector (HEC). note: export throughput is rate-limited — we'll share the recommended batching settings.
[01:48] Rajiv Kumar: about PII/PIA concerns — are payloads stripped? do you include request/response bodies?
[01:54] Sana Patel: by default we capture metadata and structured event fields; we do not include full request/response bodies in audit logs unless explicitly enabled. for example, an admin who exports a model evaluation artifact will have an event with the artifact id and size but not the contents. you can enable additional logging for debug but that should be governed by your policies.
[02:15] [02:15] Emily Park: do you support Customer-Managed KMS?
[02:18] Sana Patel: yes — at-rest encryption uses AES-256 by default and for enterprise customers we offer customer-managed keys (CMKs) through major cloud KMS providers. keys can be rotated per your policy and we log key rotation events in audit logs (who rotated, when).
[02:31] Rajiv Kumar: is the export encrypted in transit?
[02:33] Liam O'Connor: all exports use TLS. for S3 we support server-side encryption with customer keys (SSE-C/SSE-KMS) and we can sign objects. for syslog/HEC we use TLS mutual auth where required.
[02:47] Carlos Mendez: how granular are the RBAC roles? we need separation of duties — e.g., read-only auditors, admins, devs, platform engineers.
[02:55] Sana Patel: our RBAC model includes built-in roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Auditor, and Custom roles. you can scope roles by project, model, and environment. Auditor role is read-only with access to view logs and audit trails but cannot perform exports unless granted. we support SCIM provisioning so your identity provider can push groups and we can map to roles.
[03:18] Emily Park: SCIM sounds good — does SCIM provision group membership changes and deprovisioning?
[03:22] Sana Patel: yes, SCIM handles create/update/delete. we also support SAML SSO for interactive sessions and can log SSO assertions for traceability. small note — the transcript might have S-A-M-L spelled a few ways, sorry.
[03:36] [03:36] Rajiv Kumar: log integrity — we need tamper-evidence. any append-only or signing?
[03:41] Sana Patel: we offer an optional append-only log export to your S3 bucket with object-level manifests and hashes. we can sign manifests with our service key and also include per-batch SHA256 checksums. for higher assurance customers we recommend streaming to a customer-owned bucket and enabling object lock/retention on your side to enforce immutability.
[04:05] Emily Park: what about indexing and search? we don't want to pull raw JSON to grep every time.
[04:10] Sana Patel: for Hosted API customers we provide search and query UI in the console (indexing by timestamp, actor, event type, resource id). for large scale logs most customers forward to SIEM like Splunk/Datadog and use their search. we also provide prebuilt field mappings for Splunk so your team can drop in dashboards.
[04:28] Carlos Mendez: is there a way to correlate inference requests to audit events? for example tie a model inference token to an admin action.
[04:36] Sana Patel: yes — all request-level logs include a request_id and model_version id. admin actions that change routing or rollout include the affected request ids where applicable. correlation is possible by joining on request_id or user id. note: in some high-throughput paths we do sampling for full payloads — but metadata is always emitted.
[04:56] Rajiv Kumar: compliance — do you have SOC 2 and ISO evidence?
[04:59] Liam O'Connor: yes we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO 27001 scoping. we'll send the SOC 2 report and ISO statement of applicability. we also have PCI-adjacent controls and can talk about penetration testing cadence.
[05:12] Emily Park: retention policy question — can retention be set per project or is it account-wide?
[05:17] Sana Patel: retention can be set at the workspace/project level for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted account level is default but enterprise can request per-workspace retention in the contract.
[05:28] [05:28] Carlos Mendez: how do you handle cross-region exports? our data residency requires EU-only storage for certain environments.
[05:33] Sana Patel: we provide region-scoped logging — you can configure logs to stay in a region and we support pushing to a region-specific S3 or object store. for Private deployments you can keep logs entirely behind your VPC.
[05:46] Rajiv Kumar: any rate limits or costs for exporting logs?
[05:49] Liam O'Connor: we include baseline export throughput in enterprise tiers, above that there are additional charges. we'll share the spreadsheet with throughput and cost examples.
[06:01] Emily Park: can you redact fields before export? for example mask PII in logs?
[06:04] Sana Patel: yes — we support field-level redaction rules and PII masking on export, including hashing or tokenization. this is configurable and we will show examples in the schema doc.
[06:18] [06:18] Rajiv Kumar: audit trail retention for forensic investigations — if we need 7 years, doable?
[06:23] Sana Patel: technically yes — if you archive to your own storage (S3 glacier or equivalent) you can keep logs indefinitely. Hosted plan default won't keep that long without archive. we'll propose an architecture and cost model.
[06:36] Emily Park: do you log administrative console access via SSO?
[06:39] Sana Patel: yes — we log SSO sessions, assertion details (issuer, subject) and session start/stop. those are included in audit events.
[06:49] Carlos Mendez: who in Redwood has access to raw logs? internal access controls?
[06:53] Liam O'Connor: internal access is limited and logged. we have role-based internal permissions, break-glass procedures, and access is audited. access to customer raw logs requires approval and is logged in our internal audit trail.
[07:07] Rajiv Kumar: what about alerting on suspicious admin activity? can you integrate alerts to PagerDuty?
[07:12] Sana Patel: yes — we have built-in alert rules for anomalous admin activity and integrations to PagerDuty, Slack, and webhook sinks. customers can map events to severity and notification targets.
[07:24] Emily Park: ok let's recap next steps.
[07:27] Liam O'Connor: recap: Sana will share the audit log schema and SIEM export examples, i'll send SOC2/ISO docs, and we'll schedule the POC to stream logs to your S3 and Splunk. Carlos will confirm retention window. any other asks?
[07:43] Rajiv Kumar: one more — can you provide a sample signed manifest so we can validate checksum process?
[07:48] Sana Patel: yes i'll include a sample signed manifest and SHA256 examples in the doc pack.
[07:55] Liam O'Connor: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week.
[08:00] [08:00] Meeting ends
notes: Customer strongly focused on SIEM integration (Splunk) and retention/immutability. Interested in CMK and region-scoped storage. Raised typical enterprise questions about who can access logs and proof of tamper-evidence.
